analysis.investment_thesis: Bikaji is a genuine branded FMCG business in a segment I deeply understand — ethnic snacks with a loyal consumer base — but at 66x P/E with a 26% net profit decline in FY2025, the price demands flawless execution the company has not demonstrated. I want this business at 25-30x P/E; not here.
key_strengths: Strong consumer brand in ethnic snacks (bhujia, namkeen) with 19.5% revenue CAGR over 5 years — real market share gains
High promoter holding of 73.88% — founding family is aligned with minority shareholders
Consistent positive OCF all 5 years; low D/E of 0.19 — balance sheet discipline maintained during growth
key_risks: Net profit fell from 263 Cr (FY2024) to 194 Cr (FY2025) — a 26% decline — margin compression is real and the trend is worrying
EBITDA contracted from 415 Cr to 356 Cr in FY2025, suggesting input cost pressure or operating deleverage from expansion
Competing against HUL, ITC, PepsiCo, and Haldirams at scale — Bikaji remains a regional challenger with national ambitions that are expensive to fund
red_flags: 66x P/E with declining profits is a dangerous combination — there is no margin of safety at this price
Borrowings nearly doubled from 166 Cr to 310 Cr in FY2025 precisely when profits fell — using debt to fund expansion during a weak year is not a trait I reward
EBITDA margin declining: 415 Cr on 2,329 Cr revenue (FY2024) vs 356 Cr on 2,622 Cr revenue (FY2025) — growing revenue but shrinking profits is a quality concern
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bikaji has built a real brand in a category I know well — impulse, habitual snacking is as predictable as it gets in consumer behaviour. The 19.5% revenue CAGR is impressive, and the promoter's high stake signals genuine skin in the game. In isolation, the business model is one I would study seriously and potentially own at the right price.

But 66x P/E is the price of perfection, and FY2025 delivered the opposite — net profits down 26%, EBITDA contracting, borrowings rising. When I bought DVmart's early land parcels, I demanded a wide margin of safety even on businesses I loved. Here, even if Bikaji delivers a full recovery in FY2026, the forward P/E of 49x still offers no room for error. I will watch this business, wait for the margin recovery to be confirmed across two consecutive quarters, and revisit only when the stock trades at 25-30x earnings.
